To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strange quark contributions to neutrino scattering on the nucleons are significant and can be determined with a high accuracy, if the neutrino–quark scattering is well known and the strangeness form factor of the nucleon is well determined.

the strange quark contributions to physical observables by neutrino (antineu- trino) scattering on a nucleon can be sizable in the quasi- elastic region, but the uncertainties of the strangeness form factor data make it difficult to extract reliable information on the strange quark contents from the scattering.

the strangeness contents in the nucleon are not negligible for the neutrino (or antineutrino) scattering and that the neutrino–proton cross section is about 1/4 of the antineutrino–proton one in the quasi- elastic region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neutrino–(anti)neutrino scattering on the nucleons and nuclei.
the ambiguities of neutrino and antineutrino scattering due to the uncertainties in the strangeness contents of the nucleon.
the strangeness contributions to the neutrinos (antineutrinos) scattering on the free nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the strangeness contributions in the neutrino (anti-neutrino) scattering is not negligible and is important to be considered in the analysis of the scattering data.
the strangeness form factor is a crucial factor in the neutrino (anti-neutrino) scattering, and that it is necessary to have a precise measurement for the strangeness content of the nucleon.
the strangeness contents in the neutrino–(anti)neutrino scattering are not well understood yet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strangeness contents in the neutrino scattering on the nucleons are not yet fully determined, but they are still important in the neutrino–matter interaction.

there is no significant effect of the strangeness contents on the neutrino (and antineutrino) scattering observables, which is in contrast to the case of the electron scattering, where the strangeness contents can be probed.
the strangeness form factor is not well determined at the low energy region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ambiguities of strangeness contributions to the neutrinoscattering on the nucleon are not negligible and should be taken into account for the neutrino– nucleus scattering.
the neutrino–proton scattering is sensitive to the strange form factors, while the antineutrino–proton and the neutrino–neutron scatterings are not.
the neutrino (or antineutrino) scattering is sensitive to the strange contents of the nucleon, and the strangeness contents can be probed by using a combination of neutrino–electron scattering data.
